summary: Otto Benndorf was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Bonn under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker, and at Göttingen. He held posts at Göttingen, Zurich, Munich, Charles University, Vienna, and the Austrian Archaeological Institute.
Otto Blau studied at the University of Halle, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott, and the University of Leipzig.

Otto Donner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Helsinki, Berlin under Weber and Steinthal, and under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Helsinki as docent and professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology.

Otto E. Neugebauer, a scholar of history and archaeology, studied at Graz, Munich, Göttingen, and Copenhagen, and under Boris Turayev. He held positions at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Otto Fischer worked in Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen, and held posts at Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, the University of Basel, and Kunstmuseum Basel.

Otto Franke was a scholar of Sinology and Indology. He studied at Freiburg, Kiel, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn, and Berlin under Carl Arendt and Wilhelm Grube, later holding posts at Berlin, Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut, and the University of Hamburg.

Otto Fredrik Tullberg was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Uppsala and with teachers including Bopp, Kosegarten, Stenzler, Quatremère, de Sacy, Burnouf, Lassen, and Wilson, later becoming Professor of Oriental Languages at Uppsala University in 1843.
Otto Grohma was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna around 1965–1971 and served there as an assistant in 1972.

Otto Heinrich Wilhelm Keller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Freiburg and Giessen under Christian Bartholomae, later holding teaching and director posts at Gymnasium zu St. Katharinen Oppenheim, Gymnasium Michelstadt, and Wolfgang-Ernst-Gymnasium.

Otto Hoffmann was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen under August Fick. He held academic posts at the University of Königsberg, the University of Breslau, and the University of Münster.

Otto Huth was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel, Marburg, and the University of Bonn. He held posts as a Privatdozent at the University of Strasbourg and as a Privatdozent and professor at the University of Tübingen.

Otto Höfler was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Vienna under Rudolf Much, Lund, and Kiel, and held posts at Uppsala, Lund, Kiel, the University of Munich, and the University of Vienna.
Otto Jahn was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held posts at Kiel, Greifswald, Leipzig, and the University of Bonn.

Otto K. Schwarz works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation and the Russian Christian Academy for the Humanities, joining the Higher School of Economics faculty in 2026.

Otto Karow was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Tibetology who studied at Giessen, Berlin, Leipzig, and Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn, the University of Münster, and Goethe University Frankfurt.
Otto Loth specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and held a post at the University of Leipzig from around 1874 to 1881.

Otto Maenchen-Helfen worked in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and archaeology. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady, and held posts at the Marx-Engels Institute, Berlin, Mills College, and UC Berkeley.

Otto Rosenberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at Saint Petersburg under Shcherbatskoy and Oldenburg, and at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Otto Schlaginhaufen studied at the University of Zurich, where he earned a Ph.D. He held posts at the Rudolf-Virchow-Sammlung, the Museum of Ethnology in Dresden, and as an assistant and professor of anthropology at the University of Zurich.

Otto Schrader was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jena, Leipzig, and Berlin. He served as an Oberlehrer at Carolo-Alexandrinum Jena and held professorships in Indogermanistik at the University of Jena and the University of Breslau.
